data.claude-code#Claude Code source: With Credential = {“source”: “claude-code”} the plugin reads Claude Code’s own login at fetch time (macOS Keychain item Claude Code-credentials via /usr/bin/security, else ~/.claude/.credentials.json) and calls GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with the bearer token and anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20 — the same request Claude Code makes — returning every window the response carries (v0.2.0): each top-level value shaped {utilization, resets_at} (known keys keep the panel’s labels and order, an unknown key such as seven_day_oauth_apps gets a derived label) and each limits[] entry, de-duplicated by an explicit key rather than by label; a window with a null utilization is kept as n/a with a warning saying why. “view”: “overlay” in the credential returns exactly the rows of the VS Code Account & usage panel (Session (5hr), Weekly (7 day), Weekly Sonnet, Weekly ) for the equality check, and plugin-claude –raw-usage prints the response body. It never refreshes or rotates the token (an expired one is reported as “token expired, open Claude Code”), holds it in a secret.Secret, redacts it from every error, talks to that one host over TLS 1.2+ with no redirects and a 1 MiB response cap, and has fuzz targets for both decoders.
data.highlights#Highlights: GET /api/organizations/{org_uuid}/usage, cookie-authenticated, found by watching a real session’s own network traffic. Needs org_uuid alongside the cookie jar — captured once at onboarding time, since no scripted request can rediscover it from cookies alone. Talks to claude.ai over a TLS-fingerprinted (go-browserhttp) client for the one authenticated JSON call — login itself needs a real browser, this doesn’t. A credential missing org_uuid fails clearly rather than guessing.
data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-aiquota/plugin-claude Requires Go 1.26.4 or newer.
data.plugin-claude#plugin-claude:
The reference QuotaProvider plugin — Claude Max / Team Premium / Team Standard.
Calls the same undocumented endpoint claude.ai’s own web app calls to show the usage bar under Settings → Usage, authenticated purely by the account’s session cookies. Because claude.ai’s login sits behind Cloudflare’s interactive JS challenge, onboarding always drives a real embedded browser — the plugin itself only ever sees the resulting cookies and org UUID.

data.highlights#Highlights: quotapb.QuotaProviderServer: Describe (identity + login URL) and FetchQuota. A credential is map (a whole cookie jar), not one opaque string. secret.Secret — the only way to read it back is Secret.Reveal(func(string)). redact — shape-based scrubbing for text that isn’t already Secret-wrapped. AutoMTLS on every plugin connection — nothing crosses the loopback socket in the clear.
data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-aiquota/proto Requires Go 1.26.4 or newer.
data.proto#proto:
The QuotaProvider gRPC contract, plus Secret/redact credential-safety types.
A hashicorp/go-plugin service (Describe + FetchQuota) with AutoMTLS so a credential never crosses the loopback socket in the clear, plus secret.Secret (a value that can’t accidentally print via %v, a wrapped error, or JSON) and shape-based redact text scrubbing as a second line of defense over raw text that isn’t already wrapped.

data.cli#Command line: aiquota and quotaclaim:
aiquota status [–account A] [-o json|text|statusbar] loads the Claude plugin and asks live for every window (5 h session, weekly, any per-model window), printing used %, the reset time (local, 24 h) and the plan. Exit status: 0 available, 1 exhausted, 3 UNKNOWN (could not read — never reported as available or exhausted), 2 usage error. Every run writes a stamp (time, windows, verdicts, no credential) to os.UserConfigDir()/aiquota/last-status.json.
One reading for every process (v0.7.1). The usage endpoint rate limits, and a machine runs several editor windows, the CLI and the quotaclaim gate, so they share one reading kept next to the stamp (cache-*.json, no credential): within –min-interval (default 1 minute) a process reuses the last good reading and shows its real measurement time; one process at a time fetches (a lock file); a Retry-After is written down and honoured by all of them; and while the endpoint cannot be asked the last good reading is served marked stale (its age shown) for up to –max-stale (default 10 minutes), after which the answer is UNKNOWN. –fresh fetches now, still respecting a Retry-After; –min-interval 0 disables sharing. quotaclaim still checks its max-age against the real measurement time.
-o statusbar (v0.3.0, colours since v0.4.0) prints one JSON object {version, text, tooltip, level, verdict} for an editor status bar: text is Claude 30% · 5% (session · weekly) or Claude ? when UNKNOWN (the reasons are in the tooltip, never a number); level is ok, warn, error or unknown (–warn 75, –critical 90 on the worst window; an exhausted window is always error). A client asks for the contract it understands with –format-version: 1 (the default, exactly the object above) or 2 (v0.5.0), which also carries items, one per window (session, weekly, and every other window the endpoint returns, a 0 % one included), each with text, percent, band (0 to 7, equal steps of 12.5 %; –bands N, 2 to 8, for coarser steps; -1 when unknown), color (hex) and background (none, warning, error). The 8 steps are light green, dark green, light yellow, dark yellow, light orange, dark orange, then the theme’s warning and error backgrounds: VS Code’s extension API honours only those two backgrounds, so every other step is a text colour with WCAG contrast of at least 3:1 against the default status bar (#007ACC in Dark+ and Light+, #68217A with no folder), asserted by a Go test. The VS Code extension is its consumer.
quotaclaim is a Claude Code Stop / SubagentStop hook that refuses a reply asserting a usage-limit state (“weekly limit”, “hit your limit”, “resets Nov 12”, “limite hebdomadaire”, “bloqué jusqu’au”) unless a stamp younger than –max-age (default 10 minutes) backs it; it blocks with the reason naming aiquota status. An unknown stamp backs neither “available” nor “exhausted”.
The matcher claims only statements about Claude’s own usage (“5-hour limit”, “weekly limit”, “limite hebdomadaire”, “hit your … limit”, “usage limit”, “quota Claude”). Gateway vocabulary (soft/hard quota, rate_limit_exceeded, Retry-After, budgets, GitHub API rate limits) and denials are never claims. With no usable measurement (none, stale, UNKNOWN) a claim passes only if its own sentence says “unknown” or “not measured”. quotaclaim scan replays the matcher over ~/.claude/projects (read-only).
aiquota status keeps the plugin client’s own log (handshake, mTLS, stdio) quiet at Warn; –debug shows it on stderr for diagnosis.
By default aiquota status shows every window the usage endpoint returns (v0.7.0): it queries Claude Code’s own login (plugin-claude’s “Claude Code” source) and prints known windows with the panel’s labels, order, whole percentages and reset wording (Session (5hr) 37% Resets at 14:00, Weekly (7 day) 52% Resets Thu, Nov 12 at 03:00, …), Opus included, plus any other window with a label derived from its key and any limits[] entry the top level did not already report. A window listed without a value is – with verdict n/a: never a number, and outside the overall verdict. –overlay reproduces exactly the rows of the VS Code extension’s Account & usage panel, so the two compare line by line, and -o json –raw prints the usage response as received (it holds no credential). Stored claude.ai accounts are the fallback when no Claude Code login exists, or are selected with –account. The token is never refreshed (Claude Code renews its own login): once expired the status is UNKNOWN, “token expired, open Claude Code”. The read goes through /usr/bin/security, which the Keychain item’s ACL already trusts, so there is no dialog and nothing to re-approve after a reinstall.
Install without Go (since v0.8.0; v0.8.2 is the latest, and every archive is run on a real runner before it is published, aiquota --version and the plugin’s included). Each release carries one archive per platform, aiquota___.tar.gz (.zip on Windows), for Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, OpenBSD and NetBSD, amd64 and arm64, plus SHA256SUMS and a GitHub provenance attestation. An archive holds aiquota, quotaclaim and go-aiquota-plugin-claude (the Claude provider aiquota starts, looked up on PATH under that exact name): put the three in one folder on your PATH after checking the archive against SHA256SUMS. CI builds all twelve on every pull request, but only Linux, macOS and Windows are tested on a runner; the three BSDs are built and never run. For the VS Code side, see the vscode-statusbar install guide.
Install with Go, the plugin being a separate module (go install names it plugin-claude: rename it to go-aiquota-plugin-claude):
GOBIN=~/.local/bin go install github.com/go-aiquota/tray/cmd/aiquota@latest GOBIN=~/.local/bin go install github.com/go-aiquota/tray/cmd/quotaclaim@latest GOBIN=~/.local/bin go install github.com/go-aiquota/plugin-claude@latest mv ~/.local/bin/plugin-claude ~/.local/bin/go-aiquota-plugin-claude Hook configuration (~/.claude/settings.json):
{"hooks": { "Stop": [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "~/.local/bin/quotaclaim"}]}], "SubagentStop": [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "~/.local/bin/quotaclaim"}]}] }}
data.highlights#Highlights: One tray item per account, text-only (no icon clutter) — session%/weekly%. Plugin manager: launches and polls provider subprocesses over gRPC. Per-account isolated onboarding (WKWebView non-persistent data store on macOS). A credential never touches accounts.json — metadata only, OS keyring for the rest. Testable end-to-end without a mouse: the tray’s own state machine is driven by the exact call (MenuItem.Activate()) a real click makes.
data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-aiquota/tray Requires Go 1.26.4 or newer.
data.tray#tray:
The menu-bar host app — per-account tray items, plugin manager, isolated onboarding.
Renders one tray item per account (a Stats-style “46%/10%" text display), launches and polls each account’s provider plugin over the go-aiquota/proto gRPC contract, and drives a per-account isolated embedded-browser window (a fresh, non-persistent data store each time) for onboarding — so no cookie is ever copied out of a real browser by hand.

data.design#Design: VS Code extensions must be JavaScript, so the extension is a thin shell: it runs aiquota status -o statusbar --render 1 and draws exactly the items that description lists (per item id, text, tooltip, color, background, priority, alignment, command, plus a detail text and poll_seconds). Reading the credential, verdicts, thresholds, bands, colours, labels and the item list stay in the Go binary (aiquota v0.6.0 or newer; the extension keeps asking for render 1, so a newer binary keeps working), tested there; whatever fails, the item reads Claude ? and never goes empty; no secret passes through the extension. One process at a time, killed on timeout; a 60 s interval (minimum 30 s) and a cooldown that also covers clicks keep the usage endpoint from being hammered.
data.install#Install:
Written for someone who uses VS Code and nothing else (no Go, Node or git). The full guide, with every per-OS detail, is the README’s Install section; in short:
Prerequisites. The Claude Code extension (or CLI) signed in, as the same operating-system user that will run aiquota: it reads that login (macOS Keychain item Claude Code-credentials, or ~/.claude/.credentials.json / $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) and sends it only to api.anthropic.com. Nothing passes through the extension. With Remote - SSH, WSL or Dev Containers, do it on the remote machine. Install aiquota. Download the archive for your system from the aiquota releases (aiquota___.tar.gz, .zip on Windows; Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, OpenBSD and NetBSD, amd64 and arm64) and SHA256SUMS, and check the archive against it (shasum -a 256 -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS, or Get-FileHash on Windows). Put aiquota and go-aiquota-plugin-claude (the provider plugin aiquota starts) in one folder: ~/.local/bin is searched first, then $GOBIN, $GOPATH/bin, ~/go/bin (Windows: aiquota.exe, also %LOCALAPPDATA%\aiquota); for any other folder set aiquota.binaryPath to the full path of aiquota. On macOS a browser download is quarantined: xattr -d com.apple.quarantine on both files. With Go instead: go install github.com/go-aiquota/tray/cmd/aiquota@latest and go install github.com/go-aiquota/plugin-claude@latest, the latter renamed to go-aiquota-plugin-claude. Linux, macOS and Windows are tested by CI on a runner of their own; the BSD binaries are built on every change but never run. Install the extension. It is not on the Marketplace or Open VSX. Download aiquota-statusbar-.vsix from the releases, then in the Extensions view open the ... menu, Install from VSIX…, and pick it; or run code --install-extension aiquota-statusbar-.vsix. Check. aiquota status in a terminal prints your account and one line per window; the status bar shows one item per window. A grey Claude ? carries the reason in its tooltip (aiquota not found at , no go-aiquota-plugin-claude on PATH, token expired, open Claude Code). Update by installing the newer .vsix the same way and replacing the two programs; uninstall from the Extensions view and delete the programs.
Settings: aiquota.binaryPath (default: the first aiquota found in the folders above), aiquota.intervalSeconds, aiquota.cooldownSeconds, aiquota.timeoutSeconds, aiquota.bands, aiquota.statusbar.alignment and aiquota.statusbar.priority (the items take that base priority minus 0.001 steps so they stay contiguous), aiquota.warnPercent, aiquota.criticalPercent. After installing a new version, run “Developer: Reload Window”.
data.tuning#Changing the look: edit Go, go in: The extension is a frozen, generic renderer (v0.3.2 is the latest, installed in a real VS Code by CI): the number of items, their order, labels, colours, bands, click actions, thresholds and the poll interval all come from aiquota. To change any of them, edit aiquota in tray, go install it, then click the item or run “aiquota: Refresh now” (or wait one poll). No window reload is needed, which matters because a reload restarts the extension host that every extension of the window, Claude Code included, shares; VS Code has no per-extension restart. The settings warnPercent, criticalPercent, bands and intervalSeconds are passed to the binary only when you set them; otherwise its defaults rule.
data.vscode-statusbar#vscode-statusbar:
A VS Code status bar item that always shows the Claude usage aiquota measures: the same numbers as the Claude Code extension’s Account & usage view, visible permanently instead of scrolling away.
It shows one item per window, Claude 5h 57% and 7d 10%, then each other window the provider returns (a per-model weekly window such as Fable, a 0 % one included), each coloured by its own band so the colour tells which window is hot. Hover for every window, its reset time, the plan and the measurement time; click for the detail in the “aiquota” output channel.
The scale has 8 equal steps of 12.5 % (aiquota.bands for fewer): light green, dark green, light yellow, dark yellow, light orange, dark orange, then the theme’s warning background (75 to 87.5 %) and error background (from 87.5 %). VS Code lets an extension use only those two backgrounds (StatusBarItem.backgroundColor), so every other step is a text colour with WCAG contrast of at least 3:1 against the default status bar (#007ACC in Dark+ and Light+, #68217A with no folder), asserted by a test in tray. On that mid-blue bar a text colour cannot be dark, so a “dark” step is the more saturated one. When the usage cannot be read it shows a grey Claude ? with the reason in the tooltip, never a stale number.
